title: Prefix sums & difference arrays (Depth Pass)
relevance: High — once the template ladder is done, OA/Div2 C–D still hide prefix rewrites (median gather, ratio counts, BS+diff, 2D imos); this list is the post-famous band through CM.
company_notes: Minimum cost to gather special indices → Arranging The Sheep / median + prefix (Amazon/Google OA flavor). Timestamped login/logout histograms → ABC221 D / Covered Points (imos + compression). First query index when every watched segment is satisfied → Tracking Segments (BS + diff). Maximize median of a long enough window → Max Median (BS-on-answer + ±1 prefixes).

phases.goal: Spot depth prefix/imos problems that need a rewrite before the base range-sum or difference template applies.

must_hit.point: Recognize when many static range questions, many offline range adds, or count-subarrays properties expressible from pref[r]−pref[l−1] appear under contest packing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names static ranges, offline range adds, or a property checkable from pref[r]−pref[l−1] as the cue.

must_hit.point: Statements force a rewrite first: gather cost → median + prefix counts; good cuts → prefix of runs; coverage histograms → compressed sweep; median/subarray tricks → map values to ±1 and track prefix minima; 2D paint/paths → inclusion–exclusion or cascade diffs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those rewrites before coding a plain prefix or imos.

must_hit.point: Same engines as the base topic — range aggregates via prefixes, range updates via difference/imos — but the ask is hidden until the invariant is rewritten.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says the engines are still prefix aggregates / difference updates after the rewrite.

probes: What tells you this is a prefix/imos depth problem rather than a plain array scan or segment tree?
Which rewrite does the statement force: median gather, ratio counts, compressed coverage, ±1 median check, or 2D paint/cascade?

hints.1: Ask whether the property can be phrased with range aggregates or offline range adds.
hints.2: Look for a forced rewrite: median/gather, runs, coverage histogram, ±1 median, or 2D paint.
hints.3: Say: static ranges / offline adds / pref[r]−pref[l−1] subarray counts under contest packing, after rewriting to a prefix invariant.

phases.goal: Choose the right depth rewrite: compressed imos, constructive diff, BS+diff, ±1 order stats, pref/suf transforms, or nested prefixes.

must_hit.point: Compressed sweep: emit +1 at l and −1 at r+1 on a sorted coordinate list; between consecutive events coverage is constant — multiply length by coverage, never loop the axis.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places +1/−1 events, sorts coordinates, and multiplies gap length by current coverage.

must_hit.point: BS + difference: binary-search the first moment a segment becomes full; for a mid, apply the first mid point updates on a diff array and prefix-check each segment’s coverage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Binary-searches time, rebuilds coverage with the first mid updates, and prefix-checks segments.

must_hit.point: ±1 prefix for order statistics: replace ≥x by +1 else −1; a subarray median ≥x iff some prefix difference is positive (or a prefix minimum stays controlled); init map/min carefully at index 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the threshold check to a ±1 array and argues via prefix differences or controlled prefix minima with a careful index-0 init.

must_hit.point: Contribution / constructive diff: mark the derivative of the desired contribution array, then prefix once — build the array that induces the scores, not the scores themselves.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes writing difference marks for the target contribution and recovering the array with one prefix.

must_hit.point: Pref/suf of b[i]+i and b[i]−i: a length-3 score b[i]+b[j]+b[k]-(k−i) splits into independent left/right maxima — classic prefix of transformed values.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits the length-3 score into left/right maxima of b[i]+i and b[i]−i style transforms.

must_hit.point: Nested prefixes: answers are prefixes of the prefix-sum array — precompute pref, prefpref, and sometimes i·pref[i] closed forms for sum-of-subarray-sums queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names pref/prefpref (and optionally i·pref[i]) for range sums of all subarray sums.

probes: For coverage histograms on a large axis, how do you use difference events without looping every coordinate?
How do you combine binary search with a difference array to find the first time a segment is full?
How does a ±1 rewrite turn “median ≥ x” into a prefix check?

hints.1: Decide compressed imos vs BS+diff vs ±1 median vs constructive/nested prefixes before coding.
hints.2: Coverage → +1 at l, −1 at r+1, multiply gaps; time/threshold → BS then one diff rebuild; median → ±1 and prefix min/diff.
hints.3: Also: constructive derivative-then-prefix; Running Miles pref/suf of b[i]±i; Sums of Segments via pref/prefpref.

phases.goal: Show concrete imos/prefix mechanics for compressed events, dual pref/suf aggregates, 2D marks, and CF hygiene.

must_hit.point: Compressed difference/imos: sort events (pos,+v)/(pos+1,−v); multiply gap length by current coverage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds sorted open/close events and accumulates answer as gap_length × coverage.

must_hit.point: Maintain both prefix and suffix aggregates (min/max, b[i]+i, b[i]−i) when the optimum splits into left + pivot + right.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Precomputes left and right aggregates of the transformed values and combines around a pivot.

must_hit.point: Always long long on CF; clamp r+1; for compression include r+1 as a coordinate so open/close events stay correct.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses long long, clamps r+1, and puts r+1 into the compressed coordinate list.

must_hit.point: 2D cascade/diagonal update: still O(1) marks on a 2D difference (or two 1D diffs on diagonals), then one prefix rebuild — same imos idea as timeline compression.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places O(1) 2D (or diagonal) difference marks and rebuilds with one prefix pass.

must_hit.point: Zero-Sum Prefixes: between editable zeros the running prefix is fixed; greedily set the next zero so the most frequent prefix in the segment becomes 0 (freq map of prefixes).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses a prefix frequency map between zeros and rewrites the next zero toward the mode prefix.

probes: Walk through the compressed imos event list and how you turn gaps into coverage counts.
What do you store on both sides when the score splits into left + pivot + right?
What CF-specific hygiene do you apply around r+1 and types?

hints.1: Start from sorted +v/−v events and a running coverage.
hints.2: Answer adds gap×coverage; keep pref and suf transforms when the optimum splits three ways; use long long and include r+1.
hints.3: Also: O(1) 2D/diagonal imos marks then one rebuild; Zero-Sum Prefixes greedy via prefix freq between zeros.

phases.goal: Keep depth solutions on compressed sweeps / one rebuilds / O(1) imos marks — not axis loops or segment trees.

must_hit.point: Compressed sweep never loops the axis: between consecutive events coverage is constant, so multiply length by coverage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses per-coordinate axis loops and charges work to consecutive compressed events only.

must_hit.point: 2D rectangle paint counts, value-grid rectangle sums, and cascade/diagonal updates are still inclusion–exclusion or 2D imos — not a segment tree; cascade marks are O(1) then one prefix rebuild.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses inclusion–exclusion or 2D imos with O(1) marks plus one rebuild instead of a segment tree.

must_hit.point: Binary search on time / length / threshold plus one difference rebuild to validate is the standard CF C/D combo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States BS on the answer axis with a single diff-array rebuild per mid check.

probes: Why is looping the full coordinate axis the wrong complexity move for Covered Points-style histograms?
When do you use 2D imos / inclusion–exclusion instead of reaching for a segment tree?
What work do you redo on each mid in a BS + difference solution?

hints.1: Ask whether coverage is constant between compressed events.
hints.2: Multiply gap×coverage; use O(1) imos marks + one prefix rebuild; BS reuses one diff rebuild per mid.
hints.3: Cite never looping the axis, 2D imos not segtree, and BS + one difference rebuild as the CF C/D pattern.

phases.goal: Catch sentinel, compression-endpoint, type, and wrong-structure mistakes the depth ladder punishes.

must_hit.point: For ±1 order-statistic prefixes, init map/min carefully at index 0; hash frequencies carefully with a 0 sentinel.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions an explicit index-0 / empty-prefix sentinel before scanning ±1 prefixes.

must_hit.point: Always long long on CF; clamp r+1; for compression include r+1 as a coordinate so open/close events stay correct.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Catches missing r+1 in the coordinate list, unclamped r+1, or int overflow on CF prefixes.

must_hit.point: Do not loop the coverage axis; between consecutive events multiply length by coverage.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects a per-point axis walk to gap_length × coverage on the compressed event list.

must_hit.point: Do not reach for a segment tree on 2D paint/paths or cascade/diagonal updates when inclusion–exclusion or 2D imos suffices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Redirects from segtree to inclusion–exclusion or 2D difference marks plus one prefix rebuild.

probes: What breaks if you omit the empty-prefix sentinel on a ±1 median check?
What goes wrong if r+1 is missing from coordinate compression?
When is a segment tree the wrong tool for a 2D paint or cascade update?

hints.1: Check sentinels, r+1 endpoints, and whether an axis loop or segtree appeared.
hints.2: Init at index 0 / hash with a 0 sentinel; include and clamp r+1; multiply gaps instead of looping.
hints.3: Also refuse segtree for 2D paint/cascade when inclusion–exclusion or O(1) imos marks plus one rebuild work.

tradeoffs.topic: Compressed sweep (gap × coverage) vs looping the axis
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Emit +1 at l and −1 at r+1 on a sorted coordinate list; between consecutive events coverage is constant — multiply length by coverage, never loop the axis (Covered Points / Snuke Prime).

tradeoffs.topic: Constructive difference vs building subarray-sum scores directly
tradeoffs.strong_answer: To force subarray-sum scores, mark the derivative of the desired contribution array, then prefix once — build the array that induces the scores, not the scores themselves (Sum on Subarrays).

tradeoffs.topic: Binary search + difference rebuild vs one-pass coverage
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When you need the first moment a segment becomes full, binary-search that moment; for a mid, apply the first mid point updates on a diff array and prefix-check each segment’s coverage (Tracking Segments).

tradeoffs.topic: ±1 prefix / BS+±1 minima vs computing medians directly
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Replace ≥x by +1 else −1; a subarray median ≥x iff some prefix difference is positive or a prefix minimum stays controlled — used for Median on Segments and Max Median (BS on answer + ±1 prefix minima).

tradeoffs.topic: Pref/suf of b[i]±i vs searching all length-3 triples
tradeoffs.strong_answer: A length-3 score b[i]+b[j]+b[k]-(k−i) splits into independent left/right maxima via prefixes/suffixes of b[i]+i and b[i]−i (Running Miles).
Rectangle paint counts, value-grid rectangle sums, and cascade/diagonal updates are still inclusion–exclusion or 2D imos (O(1) marks then one prefix rebuild) — not a segment tree.

gotchas.trap: Omitting the empty-prefix sentinel when using ±1 prefixes for median / order statistics.
gotchas.correction: Init map/min carefully at index 0; hash frequencies carefully with a 0 sentinel.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting r+1 when clamping or compressing open/close coverage events.
gotchas.correction: Clamp r+1; for compression include r+1 as a coordinate so open/close events stay correct.

gotchas.trap: Looping every coordinate on a large coverage axis.
gotchas.correction: Sort compressed events; between consecutive events multiply length by coverage.

gotchas.trap: Reaching for a segment tree on 2D paint, value-grid sums, or diagonal cascade updates.
gotchas.correction: Use inclusion–exclusion or 2D imos — cascade/diagonal updates are still O(1) marks then one prefix rebuild.

gotchas.trap: Using int aggregates on Codeforces prefix/imos problems.
Coding the base prefix/diff template before rewriting the ask.
gotchas.correction: Rewrite to a prefix invariant first: median gather, ratio a:b, coverage counts, median ≥ x, or sum-of-subarray-sums.
